question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -1 \\ -5\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_3=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{bmatrix}.
$$

For real $x_1,x_2,x_3$, use row reduction to analyze $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$. Which statements are true?

I. The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3$ are linearly independent.

II. The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3$ are linearly dependent.

III. The equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ has infinitely many solutions with coefficients not all zero.

Choose the correct combination.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Place the three vectors in the columns of the coefficient matrix. The homogeneous equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ corresponds to

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_1-2x_2-2x_3 &=0 \\ x_1-x_2 &=0 \\ 2x_1-5x_2-5x_3 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Append the zero right-hand side and use the following row operations in order.

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -5 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -5 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-2R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3+R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The pivot columns are $1,2,3$. Back substitution, beginning with the last row, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_3=0 \\ x_2+2x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_2=0 \\ x_1-2x_2-2x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1=0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $x_1=x_2=x_3=0$ is the only solution. The vectors are **linearly independent**; there is no nontrivial solution and no free variable.

I is true. II is false. III is false. Choose “I only”.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: None of the statements are true

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_3=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

For real $x_1,x_2,x_3$, use row reduction to analyze $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$. Which statements are true?

I. The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3$ are linearly independent.

II. The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3$ are linearly dependent.

III. The equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ has infinitely many solutions with coefficients not all zero.

Choose the correct combination.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Place the three vectors in the columns of the coefficient matrix. The homogeneous equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ corresponds to

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_1+x_2-2x_3 &=0 \\ 2x_1+3x_2-2x_3 &=0 \\ -2x_1-3x_2+2x_3 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Append the zero right-hand side and use the following row operations in order.

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & -3 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-2R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & -3 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3+2R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3+R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The pivot columns are $1,2$. The variable $x_3$ is free. Set $x_3=t$ and back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_3&=t \\ x_2+2x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_2=-2t \\ x_1+x_2-2x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1=4t\end{aligned}
$$

Hence

$$
(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(4t,-2t,t),\qquad t\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

For every $t\ne0$, the coefficients are not all zero. Therefore there are infinitely many nontrivial solutions, and the vectors are **linearly dependent**. A zero final row imposes no additional constraint.

I is false. II is true. III is true. Choose “II and III only”.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: None of the statements are true

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_3=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

For real $x_1,x_2,x_3$, use row reduction to analyze $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$. Which statements are true?

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Place the three vectors in the columns of the coefficient matrix. The homogeneous equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ corresponds to

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_1-2x_2+2x_3 &=0 \\ -x_1+3x_2 &=0 \\ -2x_1+5x_2-3x_3 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Append the zero right-hand side and use the following row operations in order.

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & -3 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2+R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & -3 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3+2R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The pivot columns are $1,2,3$. Back substitution, beginning with the last row, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_3=0 \\ x_2+2x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_2=0 \\ x_1-2x_2+2x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1=0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $x_1=x_2=x_3=0$ is the only solution. The vectors are **linearly independent**; there is no nontrivial solution and no free variable.

Every column of the coefficient matrix contains a pivot in row echelon form. This is true. The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3$ are linearly dependent. This is false. The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3$ are linearly independent. This is true. “None of the above” is false.

:question/answer-fields.:answer-field/key: Every column of the coefficient matrix contains a pivot in row echelon form.
